text:
mike: Heads up — after the kernel selector update on canary, eu-west is showing a 12-18% drop in prefix cache hit-rate for short-chat prefixes. Origin QPS spiked.
elenah: Ugh. Which selector change? Was this the heuristic for fused-attn kernels? :thinking:
mike: yeah. selector moved us to fused-attn-v2 for models with seq_len <= 128. CPU/GPU profiles looked good, but KV cache usage patterns changed.
raj: got logs? p50/p95 and kv-hit breakdown by route would help. Also what batching heuristic was live on canary? (continuous-batching v3?)
mike: attaching small excerpt from profiler and cache counters:

```
# runtime perf snapshot 2001234567
model: rw-13b-fp16
kernel_selector: fused-attn-v2
batching: continuous-v3 (max_tokens=2048, batch_timeout_ms=8)
kv_cache_hits_total: 1_328_412
kv_cache_misses_total: 312_784
prefix_hit_rate: 0.809
region: eu-west
prev_prefix_hit_rate (baseline): 0.93
p50_latency_tokens: 42ms
p95_latency_tokens: 275ms
```

mike: interesting part is the per-prefix key distribution — seems more keys are hashed to longer cache lines after the kernel change (affects key normalization path).
elenah: could be key serialization order changed inside the kernel path, producing different cache keys (or TTL propagation skipped). Any diffs in key hashing? Can you diff the keying code between selectors?
raj: I instrumented keyhash in staging yesterday; fused-attn-v2 flipped a helper to use length-prefixed serialization instead of canonical tuple. That would change cache keys for any prompt with trailing metadata (routing tags, locale).
sara: If keys are different, we either lose hits or end up with duplicate entries across regions. That explains eu-west drop if walkbacks send different metadata tags per region.
perf-bot: alert: prefix-cache-hitrate-eu-west dropped 15% (window=5m) at 2001234578
ops-bot: deploy-bot: kernel-selector rolled to canary at 2001234500 (commit abcdef)
mike: plan: 1) confirm key serialization mismatch, 2) run histogram of key prefixes to see entropy shift, 3) if confirmed, roll back selector on canary and patch key normalization to be selector-agnostic.\nelenah: for multi-region impact, also check replication/coherency TTLs. If we ended up with duplicated keys, replication might treat them as distinct and blow up storage and warmup time.
raj: quick repro: ran a synthetic workload that includes routing tag "region=eu" vs absent. With fused-attn-v2 we saw a 3x higher unique-key count for same prefix set.

```
# synthetic run
unique_keys_before: 12_100
unique_keys_after: 36_512
replication_write_ops +230%
```

sara: mitigation ideas: 1) temporary sticky-routing to avoid cross-region writes, 2) increase replication async window so cold-region warmup doesn't thrash origin, 3) prefetch priming for top 5k prefixes in eu-west.
mike: Agreed. I'm going to revert selector on canary now and kick off a priming job for eu-west top prefixes.
elenah: For the fix, I'd prefer changing the key normalization to always drop ephemeral routing tags from cache key unless explicitly opted-in. Safer long-term.
raj: +1. Also add a small unit test ensuring selector changes don't alter serialized key canonical form.
perf-bot: metric note: after rollback at 2001234602, prefix-hit-rate eu-west climbed back to 0.91 in 3m.
mike: nice. I'll open a PR for key-normalization and the test. Assigning: mike -> rollback verification + priming; elenah -> key-normalization patch; raj -> add unit + histogram dashboard; sara -> priming job and replication window tweak.
sara: I'll also add a short runbook entry under incidents/cache-regressions about how to triage keying vs kernel issues (helps oncall).
elenah: can we also add a lightweight integration test that runs selector permutations and validates cache-key invariants? Something in eng-runtime CI.
raj: yep, I'll prototype a harness that runs the serialized-key diff across selectors.
mike: awesome. Thanks all. Follow-ups: PRs expected in next 6h, priming job started, watch eu-west hit-rate for next 30m. :thumbsup!
ops-bot: note: incident ticket #INC-2143 created for cache hit-rate regression (linked to canary deploy)
mike: I'll post a short postmortem draft once we have PRs and graphs.
